author: S. R. Windham
title: Lahaina Homecoming community gathering planned for July 17-19 along Front Street
text:
The County of Maui Office of Recovery announced on June 10 that Lahaina Homecoming, a three-day community event focused on culture, connection, and recovery, will take place July 17-19, 2026, along Front Street in Lahaina.
The gathering will feature cultural experiences, storytelling, resource sharing, and programming designed to welcome people back to Lahaina. The event aims to honor the town’s heritage and strengthen ties among residents as the community continues its recovery. Applications for vendors and exhibitors are being accepted at lahainahomecoming.com through June 15. Selection notifications will be made on June 30.
“This marks an important milestone in Lahaina’s recovery,” Mayor Richard Bissen said. “While there is still much work ahead, Lahaina Homecoming provides an opportunity for our community to come together, celebrate the culture and spirit of Lahaina, strengthen connections and create meaningful opportunities for local vendors, entrepreneurs and community organizations to be part of the community’s continued recovery and future.”
The idea for the gathering originated from the Maui Economic Recovery Commission’s Healing Journey Team after conversations with families and residents in Lahaina. The event is intended to create opportunities for people to gather again while supporting healing and economic revitalization. Activities include Palengke Night on Friday evening; Pa‘ūpili Saturday during the day; Ho‘olaule‘a Saturday evening; and a final celebration Sunday evening.
Priority consideration will be given to businesses based in Lahaina, wildfire-impacted entrepreneurs, cultural practitioners, and organizations serving local families. Service providers may participate at no cost; food trucks pay $200 per evening or $500 for all three evenings; creators or retail vendors pay $150 per evening or $300 for all three evenings; there is no charge for Paʻūpili Saturday.
Lahaina Homecoming is supported by several organizations including the County of Maui Office of Recovery—created by Mayor Bissen in September 2023—and the Maui Economic Recovery Commission (ERC), which was formed after the 2023 fires as a coalition dedicated to shaping Maui’s economic future.
summary: The gathering will feature cultural experiences, storytelling, resource sharing, and programming designed to welcome people back to Lahaina. The event aims to honor the town’s heritage and strengthen ties among residents as the community continues its recovery.
